agent.problem: The card tells 1 Timothy 6:19 but also explicitly recalls 1 Timothy 6:12, where Paul told Timothy to take hold of eternal life. Its citation covers only 6:19, leaving out the earlier verse used in the comparison.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

human.problem: The card notices that "take hold" repeats from 1 Timothy 6:12, so it uses verses 12 and 19, but it cites only 1 Timothy 6:19. The citation rule says to cite from the first verse used to the last. That gives 1 Timothy 6:12-19, which pulls in many verses the card never uses and breaks the "no wider" part of the same rule.
human.question: When a story card calls back to a verse well before the one it's telling, should it cite the full range from the earlier verse to the current one, cite only the current verse and put the earlier verse inline (like the 1 Timothy 6:10 reference on stop 1, card 1), or use some other approach?
